findings.summary: INITIAL creation has no durable pending-to-earned transition, so first bootstrap and forbidden recreation are not distinguishable.
findings.evidence: 90/core-design.md:24-25,35-44,93-95 authorizes INITIAL by the #76 create operation, permits allocation, and requires earned membership for ordinary acknowledgements/source/lease credit. 90/design.md:48-49 says the created copy stays unearned until reconstruction/join, but no INITIAL completion event, stored state, RPC/CAS, or initial join is defined. Actual #76 design.md:22,53-56 retains create_operation permanently and publishes chunks with initial ISR before any physical materialization; the retained operation is not consumable bootstrap authority. #79 initialization-contract.md controls filesystem use, not per-replica first allocation. Therefore treating that existing ISR as MEMBER refuses every newly created absent chunk; treating the persisted create operation as INITIAL indefinitely permits later empty recreation and still lacks the event making a new volume usable.
findings.fix: Define the durable per-chunk/ref initial-bootstrap authority and its exact conditional pending-to-earned/consumed transition, including partial creation, lost replies, new epochs and restart. Specify how first-volume zero contents become source/ack/lease eligible and why a consumed operation can never authorize a missing earned chunk. Include contracts/gate/transaction/size hooks and separate independent simulator assertions/caught mutants for initial readiness without durable creation and replayed INITIAL recreation, with real remote/local first-attach and crash/retry tests.

findings.summary: Exact-ref tombstones and their lists have no aggregate storage/response envelope or bounded migration representation.
findings.evidence: 90/contracts.md:90-106 unions every chunk replica/move/released ref and fence holder into one tombstone with refs, pending_refs and confirmed_refs plus per-UUID charges. UUID changes prevent the former node deduplication from bounding that union. 90/budgets.md:26-42 bounds Volume responses only; :46-97 pages oversized legacy Volumes only. Actual meta/service/service.go:584-614 ListTombstones scans and returns every matching full tombstone, with no page/byte cap. Even legal new RF1/N2955 volumes can retain two distinct old UUID releases per chunk, yielding about 5911 refs and roughly 2 MiB in the two full protobuf ref projections per tombstone with maximal node names; three tombstones pending for the same current ref exceed 4 MiB. The explicitly supported N65536 legacy path can exceed that in one tombstone. 90/migration.md:53-59,98-106,131-144 nevertheless requires each whole tombstone inventory/binding item <=16 KiB and to fit one <=120-key coupled transaction; a legal large tombstone cannot satisfy that representation. Raising receive limits would violate the preserved #80 contract.
findings.fix: Give exact cleanup its own bounded persisted representation and list/page/confirmation contract, covering total per-volume ref/charge multiplicity, backend request/value limits, aggregate RPC bytes and stable incarnation/revision pagination. Adapt deletion publication, sweep/admin clients, both-backend migration inventory/conversion and capacity accounting so every admitted new/paged-legacy volume remains deletable without truncating refs or dropping charges. Specify numerical caps and boundary/+1 real transport/backend fixtures, including many tombstones for one node and repeated same-node UUID replacements. Keep dependencies read-only; assign the composition hooks to #90.

findings.summary: Enrollment cannot correct an already processed item after changed observations or failed verification.
findings.evidence: 90/migration.md:131-144 accepts only the next inventory positions, or an identical retry of the latest batch ID; it has no amendment/rebind API. :145-157 begins verification only after enroll_cursor==inventory_count, then sends a failed scan back to ENROLLING with a cursor invalidated and requires explicit correction. :164-169 also allows changed UUID observations after binding and requires quarantine/review before VERIFYING. The contracts specify neither a rewind/revision-safe rewrite of an already converted item nor an operation that records that quarantine and updates coupled refs/charges/evidence. Advancing the enrollment cursor to the end therefore removes the only defined way to repair the affected item, while a replacement enrollment job is explicitly forbidden.
findings.fix: Define a bounded conditional correction/rebind-or-quarantine operation for already inventoried/converted items, or an exact durable rewind protocol, including expected original/current hashes, evidence/observation revisions, coupled-key updates, capacity conservation, counter changes, idempotence and invalidation/restart of verification digests. Keep READY immutable. Test changed observation after binding and verification failure after the final batch through correction, restart, lost reply and successful re-verification/activation on both backends.
